data.about: A 25 by 15 metre floor slab carrying one kilonewton per square metre, and the question is what arrives at each of the four columns. The answer is a chain: area load to line load by tributary width, line load to point reactions, point reactions to the next beam down, and finally to the ground. Every rung of it has to add up to the same 506.25 kN, and the view checks that at each stage. Then task c) turns the exercise around: the biggest force is GIVEN, at 310 kN, and that single number fixes the shape of the beam’s internal arch. Drag it and watch the arch grow until it no longer fits.

data.text: subsystem B — two longitudinal beams — Ansicht 1:200, span 24.50 m

steps.caption: EX 9 task 3: a floor slab, a load per square metre, and the question of what actually arrives at each column. Follow it down one storey at a time
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: top left: the plan. A 25 by 15 metre plate rests on five transverse beams; those rest on two longitudinal beams along the long edges; those rest on four corner columns. Every load takes that route and no other
steps.title: The structure

steps.caption: the sheet gives a characteristic load; design it up. Dead load, so ×1.35 — and then the total the whole floor has to deliver to the ground, which is the number everything below has to keep adding up to
steps.title: a) The design load

steps.caption: a beam picks up everything that is nearer to it than to its neighbours, so halve the distance either side. Here that is 2.5 m each way, and the two outer beams reach the plate edge exactly — so all five carry the same 5 metre strip
steps.title: a) Tributary width

steps.caption: left: one of the five beams, with its line load. It is symmetric, so each end takes half whatever the supports are — and a beam that deep does not bend, it makes a little arch inside itself: a compression chord over the top, a tie along the soffit, and two struts down to the supports
steps.title: b) Subsystem A

steps.caption: left: the long beam, with the five A-beam reactions standing on it. They are all equal, and they are the only loads it sees — the plate never touches it
steps.title: c) What lands on subsystem B

steps.caption: now the exercise turns around. The largest force is not something you find — it is given, and it decides the drawing. The element at the support carries the reaction vertically and the thrust horizontally, so one Pythagoras gives the thrust, the thrust gives the pole, and the pole gives the arch
steps.title: c) The 310 kN fixes the shape

steps.caption: every segment carries the same horizontal thrust and its own panel’s shear, so the steepest segment — the one at the support — is the largest. That is the hint the sheet gives, and it is why the constraint could be applied there
steps.title: c) The chords

steps.caption: the same 506.25 kN at every level. That is the only reason to trust any of it — a load path that does not conserve its total has a mistake in it somewhere, and this is how you find out
steps.title: Everything, checked

data.title: EX 9.3 — one load, followed all the way down
